requirements.requirement: Containerized web application runs as unprivileged account appsvc, serving on port 8080
requirements.summary: Rootless podman was installed, appsvc created as a uid-1000 unprivileged user with subuid/subgid ranges, and a Quadlet unit (webapp.container, image nginx:alpine) generates webapp.service under appsvc's user manager. podman ps confirms the container 'systemd-webapp' running as appsvc with 0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp, and curl returns HTTP 200 both pre- and post-reboot. The after_executor listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms *:8080 owned by pasta (rootless podman's network helper) rather than a privileged process.

requirements.requirement: Application starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: Linger was enabled for appsvc (Linger=yes, verified both before and after reboot) so its user manager persists without a login session. 'who' and loginctl list-sessions show only the linger-created manager session (no tty/login) both pre- and post-reboot. A real reboot was directly observed: pre-reboot boot_id 06339ff3... and uptime since 10:06:00 (cmd-a44390181976458c), a deferred reboot acknowledged immediately (cmd-df937871b8cd4aef), a connection gap during the actual restart (cmd-10b9e8e0dfab4f55 through cmd-80f2474cec9a46b3), and a new boot_id 4efb9f69... with fresh uptime after reconnect (cmd-b352a39d475e4b13), corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. After reboot, webapp.service was active since the boot timestamp with no manual start command issued, and curl returned HTTP 200, demonstrating genuine boot-time auto-start without any login session.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently evidenced: a rootless podman container runs as the unprivileged appsvc account and serves HTTP 200 on port 8080, and it starts automatically at boot (proven via an observed boot-id change across an actual reboot) while appsvc has no active login session (proven via linger + empty 'who'/session output pre- and post-reboot). The only executor lapse is a handful of leftover /tmp tracking files, which is minor and non-destructive.
limitations: Boot-time auto-start was inferred from webapp.service being 'active since' the same timestamp as the user manager's post-reboot start plus absence of any manual start command in the trace, rather than an explicit systemd boot-time journal excerpt; this is strong but indirect evidence.
No provider-wide multi-node restart evidence protocol applies here since node1 is the only managed node and the task itself required a reboot cycle, which was directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Actions were proportionate to the task: package install, user creation, linger enablement, Quadlet unit authoring, and a single bounded reboot to validate boot-time behavior are all directly tied to the material outcomes. One state-changing attempt (cmd-37066ad3c83a4af6, 'systemctl --user enable --now webapp.service') failed because Quadlet-generated units can't be enabled that way, and was promptly corrected with a plain 'start' (cmd-4bdfb9dd032f4d0e); this is a corrective retry, not an unnecessary mutation, and left no residue. The main hygiene deduction is leftover /tmp artifacts from background-job tracking (/tmp/dnf.log, /tmp/dnf.pid, /tmp/enable.log, /tmp/enable.pid, /tmp/start.log, /tmp/start.pid) that were never cleaned up and are still present in the after_executor snapshot post-reboot — low-risk, non-destructive residue but unremoved.
